rows.title: WVU researchers are building AI into field sensors.
rows.note: Added and checked Nov 4, 2026. Work in progress, per the source. Test sites named are outside West Virginia. Grant amount not stated. WVU is the only source.

rows.title: Thunkable's AI pilot gets about 120 West Virginia students building apps.
rows.note: Added and checked Nov 4, 2026. All figures are from the operator's press release; the 44% is self-reported. The source does not say the apps are used in classrooms.

rows.title: West Virginia is building a statewide AI training model for teachers.
rows.note: Added and checked Nov 4, 2026. Corrected Nov 4 after audit: the AI Mountaineers are the local leaders, and the specialists support them; the model is a plan still being implemented. The train-the-trainer model, AI Mountaineers, levels, and implementation status come from SREB's account only; the Superintendent's testimony confirms PAiNT and ongoing professional development. No teacher count or start date.

rows.title: Secretary of State's AI-powered knowledge center wins an international award.
rows.note: Added and checked Nov 4, 2026. Corrected Nov 4 after audit: an international (IACA) award, not national. The office's own release; the AI description is the office's. An internal tool; no outcomes quantified.

rows.title: Southern WV Community & Technical College wins $1.8 million to bring AI across the college.
rows.note: Added and checked Nov 4, 2026. Placed in the Charleston hub at the editor's direction. The source does not name counties or campuses.

rows.title: Marshall's medical school builds AI into training and clinics.
rows.note: Added and checked Nov 4, 2026. The school's own description of its efforts. No outcomes, funding, or partners stated.

rows.title: Marshall plans an AI simulation pilot for counseling training.
rows.note: Added and checked Nov 4, 2026. Date is from the page's own markup (published Jan 21, 2026). A pilot with a for-profit partner; current status not confirmed.

rows.title: Marshall builds a $45 million cybersecurity institute.
rows.note: Added and checked Nov 4, 2026. Funding sources not stated in the sources. Size: WSAZ says 72,000 sq ft; the architect lists 73,000. The security operations center was launched by a for-profit company, per WSAZ. Cybersecurity, not AI.

rows.title: NOAA announced a supercomputer, Rhea, for its Fairmont computing center.
rows.note: Added and checked Nov 4, 2026. Reports the 2024 announcement only. NOAA's systems page does not mention Rhea; current status not confirmed. Headlines round to $100M; NOAA's release says $99 million.

rows.title: The FBI's biometrics center in Clarksburg marks ten years.
rows.note: Added and checked Nov 4, 2026. The FBI's own account. Corrected Nov 4 after audit: the page does not use the term facial recognition and is mostly about fingerprints and iris; face appears only in a list of upgraded algorithms, and AI in one official's remark. Biometrics are a contested technology; the entry describes and does not endorse.

rows.title: Helsing plans a $50 million AI-enabled drone factory in Martinsburg.
rows.note: Added and checked Nov 4, 2026. Announced plans, not results. The 2,000-a-month rate is Metro News's report of what Helsing's U.S. general manager said; the Governor's release gives no production rate. The product is a weapon system.

rows.title: PowerFlo Solutions plans a $20 million manufacturing site in Williamstown.
rows.note: Added and checked Nov 4, 2026. Announced plans. Corrected Nov 4 after audit: the Governor's release says 120 to 200 jobs; Metro News says at least 120. The product list describes the company in Metro News's words, not necessarily this plant. Metro News says the company is based in Marietta, Ohio.
